findings.title: Gluten-containing Choco Pie is sold as 'Sem Glúten' (health-safety misrepresentation)
findings.evidence: Product 70 title: 'Bolinho Coreano ChocoPie Orion Chocolate Duplo c/ Marshmallow | Caixa 6 un | 180g | Sem Glúten | Importado Mimos Korea'. Its description has '✅ Sem glúten', but its own attributes say 'Alérgicos': ['Contém glúten','leite','soja'] and 'Ingredientes Principais': ['Farinha de trigo', ...]. Product 259 (same SKU BLN-CHP-LT-CHC) has the same contradiction in its title ('| Sem Glúten |') and description ('✅ Sem glúten'), with attributes 'Contém glúten'. Both are in stock at R$25.90, so they are eligible to sync to Google and Meta. Google Misrepresentation policy (6150127): 'Offers that represent you or your products in a way that isn't accurate, realistic, and truthful' are not allowed. 'Violations of this policy are ... considered egregious ... your Google accounts will be suspended upon detection and without prior warning.'
findings.detail: Wheat flour is the first ingredient, so the gluten-free claim is false. It is a direct safety risk for celiac customers. The title and description say 'Sem Glúten' while the structured attributes say 'Contém glúten'. That kind of contradiction inside a listing is what Merchant Center reviewers and automated classifiers flag. Because misrepresentation is treated as egregious, the risk is suspension of the whole Merchant Center account, not only disapproval of these two items. The claim appears in the style of the new emoji/ChatGPT copy, which was applied to these two older products on or before 2026-09-12 (images 1024/1025 were added that day).
findings.recommendation: Remove 'Sem Glúten' from the titles, descriptions and short descriptions of 70 and 259 now, before any other feed work. Merge the two duplicates (see the duplicates finding). In the future content pipeline, allergen and gluten statements must come only from a verified structured field (for example allergens and contains_gluten taken from the package label) and never from generated text. Add a validator that blocks publishing when the free text contradicts the structured allergen data. Brazilian gluten-labelling law (Lei 10.674/2003) also applies; it was not fetched in this audit.

findings.title: 13 soju (alcohol) listings: prohibited in Meta Commerce, restricted on Google; 11 newer listings lack ABV and age warnings
findings.evidence: Alcohol listings: 154, 155, 156, 810, 813, 815, 817, 819, 822, 825, 827, 829, 831. Of these, 12 are in stock (all except 155). The older listings 154–156 carry attributes {'ABV':['12%'], 'Aviso':['Proibido para menores de 18 anos','beba com moderação']}. All 11 listings created 2026-08-22 (810–831) have attributes = {} and no ABV or age warning. Their copy pushes youth/fandom contexts: 'Muito popular em K-Dramas, K-Pop ... festas temáticas', 'Maratonar doramas', 'Festas K-pop', 'Happy Hour'. Product 815 (Lichia) is in categories ['Bebidas','Ofertas Mimos'] and NOT in 'Soju', so an exclusion rule based on the category would miss it. Meta Commerce Policy (facebook.com/policies_center/commerce/alcohol): 'Commerce content may not promote the buying, selling or trading of alcohol' – NOT ALLOWED: 'Alcoholic drinks of any kind'. Meta ads (transparency.meta.com): alcohol ads are allowed but 'At a minimum, ads may not be targeted to people under 18'. Google free listings alcohol policy (12077694): Brazil is 'Allowed with limitations'; not allowed: 'Show listings for alcohol to customers below the legal drinking age' and 'Imply that drinking alcohol can improve social ... standing'. Google Ads added Brazil to the approved alcohol-sale locations on 2026-07-28 (adspolicy 17230661). Brazil: Lei 13.106/2015 makes selling or delivering alcohol to minors a crime (ECA art. 243). Lei 9.294/1996 art. 1 treats drinks above 13 °GL as 'bebidas alcoólicas' for advertising restrictions.
findings.detail: Facebook for WooCommerce syncs every published product by default. If it is connected, all 13 soju items are pushed into the Meta catalog, where they violate Commerce Policy. Rejected items clutter the catalog, and repeated violations can restrict Shops or commerce features for the whole catalog. On Google the items are allowed in Brazil, but they must be correctly categorised as alcoholic beverages so Google can apply age restrictions. The copy also must not tie drinking to social success or to youth culture. The 2026 listings dropped the ABV and 'Proibido para menores de 18 anos' fields that the 2025 listings had. The descriptions of the Saero listings (819–827) do not even name the correct product line (see the content-mismatch finding). The 12% ABV stated on 154–156 could not be verified against the manufacturer.
findings.recommendation: Exclude all alcohol from Meta catalog sync: set the Facebook visibility 'Do not sync' per product, or exclude a dedicated 'Bebida alcoólica' category in the plugin settings. First fix 815's category so every soju is caught. For Google, keep the items but submit google_product_category 'Food, Beverages & Tobacco > Beverages > Alcoholic Beverages' (or make sure auto-categorisation lands there). Remove the K-pop/teen/party hooks. Add structured ABV, a +18 warning and 'beba com moderação'. Add age confirmation at checkout. In the solution's data model, make 'is_alcohol' a required flag that drives channel exclusion and the required warning fields.

findings.title: Promotional banner images ('40% de DESCONTO', 'etiqueta adesiva oferta') used as main or gallery images on 20 products
findings.evidence: There are 13 distinct promo images. Main image (becomes image_link): 890 → '40% de DESCONTO (61)' (id 891); 980 → 'Documento A4 etiqueta adesiva oferta balão divertido amarelo e vermelho (6)' (id 974); 985 → 'Documento A4 etiqueta adesiva oferta balão ...' (id 992). Gallery (becomes additional_image_link): 894/899/902 share 897 '40% de DESCONTO (61)'; 905/908/910 share 907; 912/916 share 914; 919/923 share 920; 926/932/933 share 927; 934/939 share 935; 941/946 share 942; 980 also has 976/977/978 'Documento A4 etiqueta adesiva oferta ...'. Google image_link (6324350): 'Don't use an image that contains promotional elements ... calls to action ... price information ... promotional adjectives ... Any overlay, for example, watermarks' and 'If you don't follow these requirements, your product will be disapproved'. additional_image_link (6324370): additional images must 'Meet the requirements for the image link attribute ... If you don't follow these requirements, we'll disapprove your product'. Google 13693497: products with a 'Promotional overlay on image' 'will remain disapproved until you have updated their images'.
findings.detail: Every Sakuragi product (17 items created 2026-09-02) has a discount banner in its gallery. The three backpack/sweet items above use a banner as their MAIN image. All 20 products are expected to be disapproved, or served without images, in Merchant Center. A '40% de DESCONTO' claim with no matching sale price in the feed is also a price-representation risk: the Store API snapshot only shows a single price, and no sale price was visible. Meta requires catalog images to 'accurately represent the specific product for sale'. Promo art is for ad creative, not catalog items.
findings.recommendation: Delete the banner attachments from the product galleries and use clean packshots, with the product filling 75–90% of the frame. Put discounts in the sale_price attribute or in Merchant Center Promotions, never baked into images. In the solution, classify uploads by file name and optionally by OCR or vision model, and refuse gallery images whose names match 'desconto|oferta|etiqueta|promo|%'.

findings.title: ChatGPT-generated images are the main image on 15 products (AI metadata and accuracy requirements)
findings.evidence: There are 24 distinct images named 'ChatGPT Image <date>' (for example 'ChatGPT Image 6 de ago. de 2026, 16_12_50 (1)') on 16 products. They are the MAIN image on 15: 902, 905, 908, 910, 912, 916, 919, 923, 926, 932, 933, 934, 939, 941, 946. Product 890 has two in its gallery. Product 902 has the same AI file uploaded twice (903 and 904). Google image_link and additional_image_link: 'All images created using generative AI must contain meta data indicating that the image was AI-generated (for example, the IPTC DigitalSourceType TrainedAlgorithmicMedia metadata tag). Don't remove embedded metadata tags'. Google also requires images to 'Accurately display the entire product'. Meta: 'Images must accurately represent the specific product for sale.'
findings.detail: Every Sakuragi item (the batch created 2026-09-02) is represented mainly by AI renders instead of photos of the real package. The file names alone show they were not photographed. If the renders were edited, exported, compressed, or processed by an image optimiser, the provenance metadata that Google requires is likely gone. Whether the metadata survived could not be verified without downloading the files. Generated packaging can also differ from the real product (text, weight, flavour art). That becomes a misrepresentation risk in Google and a Meta 'accurately represent' issue. For food, a customer expects to see the real label.
findings.recommendation: Replace the main images with real photos of the actual product (the multi-angle package shots Google recommends). If AI images stay in the gallery, keep the original export, verify with exiftool that IPTC DigitalSourceType=trainedAlgorithmicMedia is present, and never run them through tools that strip metadata. The solution's media intake should record a source for every asset (own photo, supplier, AI, marketplace) and block AI images from being the featured image.

findings.title: Screenshots, WhatsApp exports, thumbnails and marketplace-copied images; one image shared across different variants
findings.evidence: Screenshot 'Capturar' (843) is in the galleries of 842, 846, 849, 852, and 'Capturar' (943) in 941, 946. The main image of 948 is 'WhatsApp Image 2026-06-27 at 16.41.01'. The main image of 894 is Amazon CDN '61oMCHIuu4L._AC_UF350,350_QL50_' (a 350×350 px, quality-50 thumbnail per Amazon's URL suffix), uploaded twice as 896 and 898. 899 uses Amazon '61RZ-t7Z5SL._AC_UF894,1000_QL80_' twice (900/901). Mercado Livre CDN copies 'D_NQ_NP_2X_...-MLA...' (959–964) are shared by 957 Cinza, 967 Rosa and 968 Verde. Shopee CDN-hash files (br-11134207-...) cover 24 products. One of them (812) is shared by 6 different soju flavours (810, 813, 815, 817, 819, 831), and 824 is shared by 822/825/827/829. The generic '1' (836) and 'br-...mqbyej9kqo02df' (837) are shared by three Chuyin flavours (833/838/840). 1011 (described as 'Peso líquido: 140g') shows 'Orion-Bungo-Choco-Mochi-Soft-Cake_-174g' and 'Orion_Cham_Booner_Bbang_174g', and also has 'image (1)'. Rules: Meta image_link 'at least 500 x 500 pixels' (developer catalog fields). Google: new 'at least 500 x 500 pixels for all products beginning January 31, 2027' and 'Don't scale up an image or submit a thumbnail'. Google variants: 'Submit a unique image that represents the distinguishing details of each variant ... For variants based on color, show only one variant.'
findings.detail: Image names were the only evidence; no pixels were inspected. Still, several classes of image are unsuitable for feeds. Screenshots usually carry UI chrome or text. WhatsApp exports are recompressed. The Amazon 350 px thumbnail is below Meta's hard minimum of 500×500, so 894 would be rejected in Meta. It will also fall below Google's 500×500 minimum from 2027-01-31. Images copied from Amazon, Mercado Livre or Shopee CDNs may belong to other sellers. Their ownership is unverified and they could trigger IP complaints. Reusing one image for different flavours or colours means the feed shows the wrong variant; this breaks Google's variant image rule and Meta's 'accurately represent the specific product'. 46 of 103 products have only one image. Every image has empty alt text (103/103); that does not affect the feed but hurts SEO and accessibility.
findings.recommendation: Build an image-quality gate: minimum 1000×1000 (hard floor 500×500), a unique main image per SKU or variant, no screenshots or WhatsApp exports, and a recorded origin/licence for each asset. Replace 894's main image first, because it fails Meta today. Prefer own photos. If supplier images are used, get written permission. Fill the alt text from the structured title.

findings.title: No GTIN/EAN on any product (0/103) and no MPN, although every product is manufacturer-branded packaged goods
findings.evidence: The Store API snapshot exposes no GTIN field for any of the 103 products. Almost all are branded retail packs from Lotte, Orion, Sakuragi, Youngpoong, Yantai, Chuyin and others, which carry manufacturer barcodes. Google GTIN (6324461): 'Strongly recommended for all products with a GTIN assigned by the manufacturer ... Products with missing or incorrect GTIN [gtin] attributes may have limited visibility. Accurate matching to products can't be assured when GTIN is missing' and 'Don't guess or make up a value'. Meta catalog fields: gtin 'recommended to help classify the item'. WooCommerce 9.2 added a core 'GTIN, UPC, EAN or ISBN' field (global_unique_id), and Google for WooCommerce 2.9.0+ syncs it to Merchant Center. The GLA FAQ says identifier_exists=false logic was removed. For items without a GTIN it advises: 'MPN – Enter the product SKU used in WooCommerce; Brand – ...'.
findings.detail: Without GTINs, Google cannot match these offers to its product catalogue, which limits visibility on the whole catalogue in Shopping. Korean imports have real EAN-13 codes (typically with an 880 prefix) that can be read from the package. This must be done per variant, because each flavour has its own barcode. A GTIN also blocks duplicates: Google says 'Don't submit multiple products ... that use the same GTIN'. Caveat: the public Store API may not expose global_unique_id or the legacy _wc_gla_gtin meta, so GTINs could exist in the database. Verify this before assuming they are absent.
findings.recommendation: Check the database with SELECT post_id, meta_key, meta_value FROM wp_postmeta WHERE meta_key IN ('_global_unique_id','_wc_gla_gtin','_wc_gla_mpn'). Capture the EAN from each physical package, for example with a barcode scan in the new inventory tool, and store it in the WooCommerce core GTIN field. WooCommerce rejects duplicated GTINs, which gives a natural duplicate guard. For multipacks and kits you assembled (85, 106, 829, 831), use the individual product's GTIN plus the multipack/bundle attributes, per Google. Where no GTIN exists, send MPN (the unique SKU) plus brand.

findings.title: Brand missing on 49 products, 'Genérico' on 8, two brand terms on 33, and conflicting brands
findings.evidence: No product_brand term on 49 products: every product created from 2026-08-22 onward (833–1021, even when the title names Orion, Sakuragi, Chuyin, Yantai...). 'Genérico' on plush and slipper items 131, 135, 136, 137, 139, 140, 141, 142. Two terms (parent company plus product line, e.g. ['Lotte','Milkis'], ['Orion','Tok']) on 33 products. Conflicts: 70 and 259 have titles saying 'ChocoPie Orion' but brand 'Lotte', and image 258's file name is 'bolinho-coreano-choco-pie-lotte-...'. 864 Marine Boy has no brand, while its duplicate 150 has ['Marine Boy','Orion']. Google brand (6324351): 'Required for each product with a clearly associated brand or manufacturer ... If you don't follow these requirements, we'll disapprove your product' and 'Only provide a brand if you're sure it's correct'. GLA does not set brand automatically; it needs an attribute-mapping rule 'Taxonomies – Brands' (WooCommerce docs; WP.org support: 'Google for WooCommerce does not automatically set the brand attribute').
findings.detail: Missing brand on branded food and drink leads to disapproval or limited performance in Merchant Center, and Meta lists brand among the required catalog fields. The two-term pattern makes any taxonomy-to-brand mapping ambiguous, because a feed needs one brand string. 'Genérico' is not a brand. For those items, either leave brand empty or, if they are private-label goods, use the store name with an MPN, per Google. Orion and Lotte both sell a 'Choco Pie', so the conflict on 70 and 259 means the listing does not say which product is sold.
findings.recommendation: Normalise the brand taxonomy to one manufacturer brand per product (Lotte, Orion, Sakuragi...). Move product lines (Milkis, Pepero, O'Star, Chum-Churum, Saero) into a separate 'linha' attribute. Create the GLA attribute-mapping rule Brand ← Taxonomies – Brands. Resolve 70 and 259 by checking the physical package. Make brand a required field in the new tool, with a controlled vocabulary.

findings.title: Same physical product listed 2–3 times, with diverging prices and stock
findings.evidence: O'Star 30g Bife Americano: 237 (SKU SNK-BAT-OST-ORI-30G, R$12.90, out of stock, created 2025-11-18), 952 (no SKU, R$12.99, in stock, 2026-09-02) and 1019 (no SKU, R$12.99, in stock, 2026-09-12). 952 and 1019 have identical descriptions. O'Star 30g Queijo Duplo: 235 / 954 / 1021, the same pattern. Marine Boy Camarão 30g: 150 (R$12.90, out of stock) and 864 (R$10.99, in stock); 864 reuses 150's image attachment 228. Sac Sac Uva Verde: 242 (238 ml, R$12.90) and 253 (240 ml, R$9.99), same SKU REF-SAC-LT-238, created 8 minutes apart. Choco Pie 6 un 180g: 70 and 259, both in stock at R$25.90, same SKU. Possible: 985 (R$389.99) vs 993 (R$249.99), both black premium notebook backpacks with the same '2..7' image naming. Beyond these, 64 products share a byte-identical description with at least one other product (21 groups; for example Milkis ×6, soju 810–827 ×7). Google GTIN rule: 'Don't submit multiple products for the same country and language that use the same GTIN and have the same values for variant attributes'. Google Editorial (6150244) 'Product details' violation: 'The same product details being used for multiple products without differentiation.'
findings.detail: Google for WooCommerce creates one Merchant Center offer per WooCommerce product ID (gla_<id>). Each duplicate is therefore a separate offer competing with its twin, at different prices for the same item. Once GTINs are added, the duplicate pairs will trigger the duplicate-GTIN rule. Stock is split across records, so a customer can land on the out-of-stock twin while stock sits on the other one. The pattern is: the 2026 staff re-created items that already existed from 2025 instead of restocking or editing them.
findings.recommendation: For each cluster, choose a survivor. Prefer the oldest ID, because it keeps Merchant Center/Meta history and inbound links. Move stock, price, images and fixed content onto it. Trash the others and add 301 redirects from their permalinks to the survivor. Let GLA and Facebook for WooCommerce remove the retired items, then confirm they are gone. The new tool should run a duplicate check (normalised brand + line + flavour + size, later GTIN) before allowing a create, and offer 'restock existing' instead.

findings.title: Shared SKUs (23 products on 6 SKUs) match a raw-meta clone workflow such as Yoast Duplicate Post; 59 products have no SKU
findings.evidence: REF-MLK-LT-250 is on 67 (created 2025-11-15T21:17:26, bulk import) and on 277, 279, 281, 283, 285 (created 2025-11-19 12:56:09, 12:56:55, 12:57:50, 12:58:34, 12:59:21, roughly 45 s apart). All six have byte-identical description, short description, attributes and tags, plus weight 0.28 kg, dimensions 5×5×13, price R$12.90 and stock status out-of-stock. Only the title and featured image differ. Each image's attachment ID is the product ID + 1 (278, 280, 282, 284, 286), meaning it was uploaded while editing the new copy. The same pattern holds for BSC-PPR-LT-47G (68 → 269/271/273, 2025-11-18 22:19–22:21), BSC-ARR-ORC-ORI-129G (69 → 263/265), SNK-BAT-OST-ORI-30G (149 → 231/233/235/237, 19:31–19:36), REF-SAC-LT-238 (145 → 242/253) and BLN-CHP-LT-CHC (70 → 259). All 59 products created from 2026-08-22 have an empty SKU. Yoast Duplicate Post code: copy_post_meta_info() copies every key from get_post_custom_keys() except the default exclusion list ['_edit_lock','_edit_last','_dp_original','_dp_is_rewrite_republish_copy','_dp_has_rewrite_republish_copy','_dp_has_been_republished','_dp_creation_date_gmt'] plus the user's 'Do not copy these fields' list. Defaults: copy_thumbnail=true, copy_status=false (the copy is a draft), taxonomies copied. It writes '_dp_original' on the copy. WooCommerce's own Duplicate (WC_Admin_Duplicate_Product) instead names the copy '%s (Copy)', calls generate_unique_sku() whenever the source has a SKU, clears global_unique_id, and sets status draft. WooCommerce's product setters reject duplicated identifiers ('Invalid or duplicated GTIN...' in set_global_unique_id; set_sku uses the same uniqueness check), so the admin UI, REST API and CSV importer normally cannot create identical SKUs.
findings.detail: The observed data fits a raw post-meta clone and does not fit WooCommerce's native duplicate. _sku, _price, _stock and _stock_status, weight and dimensions, _product_attributes, the description and excerpt, and the brand, category and tag terms were all carried over. The operator then changed only the title and the featured image. WooCommerce's native duplicate would have produced REF-MLK-LT-250-1 and similar SKUs plus '(Copy)' titles. Yoast Duplicate Post is active (the duplicate-post/v1 REST namespace is exposed) and behaves exactly like this. This is an inference from public data, though: Yoast's docs say the plugin must be enabled for the 'product' post type, and another raw-meta cloner, direct SQL or WP All Import would leave the same fingerprint. The proof is the '_dp_original' meta on 277–285 and the others. Side effects of the same mechanism: (a) total_sales and _stock are copied, which distorts inventory and bestseller sorting; (b) _product_image_gallery is copied, which explains the gallery images shared across sibling products (897, 907, 914, 920, 927, 935, 942); (c) sync meta is copied. Facebook for WooCommerce strips fb_product_item_id and fb_product_group_id only through the 'woocommerce_duplicate_product_exclude_meta' filter, which runs only for WooCommerce's own duplicate. A Duplicate Post clone therefore inherits the source's Meta item IDs, and likewise _wc_gla_* such as _wc_gla_google_ids and _wc_gla_synced_at, if the source had already been synced. A clone could then be treated as already linked to the original's Google or Meta item, and deleting the clone could remove the original's item. This last effect is plausible but not verified. Shared SKUs also block Google's recommendation to 'Use the product's SKU where possible' as the ID. Meta says of duplicate IDs: 'If there are multiple instances of the same ID, we ignore all instances.'
findings.recommendation: Run these checks in the database: SELECT post_id, meta_value FROM wp_postmeta WHERE meta_key='_dp_original'; check for identical fb_product_item_id and _wc_gla_google_ids values across different post_id; and SELECT meta_value, COUNT(*) FROM wp_postmeta WHERE meta_key='_sku' AND meta_value<>'' GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(*)>1. Then either disable Duplicate Post for products, or set 'Do not copy these fields' to _sku, _global_unique_id, _stock, _stock_status, total_sales, _wc_gla_*, fb_*, _wc_facebook_*, _product_image_gallery, _wc_average_rating, _wc_review_count. Better still, have the new tool own product creation. Assign unique SKUs by a scheme such as REF-MLK-LT-250-MEL. Plan the SKU change together with the Meta resync, because the Meta retailer_id includes the SKU (see the ID-stability finding).

findings.title: Deleting and re-creating products resets Merchant Center and Meta item IDs and history; the data shows re-creation has happened
findings.evidence: ID formats: Google for WooCommerce offer ID = 'gla_' + WooCommerce product ID ('a WooCommerce product with a product ID 23 would have the ID gla_23'). 'If a synced product is deleted/trashed, it will also get removed from the Google Merchant Center.' On changing the ID: 'a different ID means a new product ... Historic reports ... would no longer match.' Facebook for WooCommerce retailer_id = '<SKU>_<product ID>', or 'wc_post_id_<product ID>' when there is no SKU (fbutils.php get_fb_retailer_id). WooCommerce doc: 'In cases where the products are entirely deleted (programmatically deleted, for example), some orphan products will remain on the FB catalog.' Google ID (6324405): 'Use a stable ID ... used to track the product's performance history ... If you change the ID, you'll overwrite your product and its history' and 'Don't recycle an ID'. Signs of re-creation in this store: attachments 221 'soju-chum-churum-lotte-blueberry-de-360ml-2' and 223 '...maca-verde...-2' were uploaded 2025-11-17 and now have no parent (unattached), yet they are the main images of 813 and 810, created 2026-08-22. The original 2025 Blueberry and Maçã Verde products no longer exist publicly. 864 (2026-08-22) reuses 150's image 228 instead of restocking 150. The ID-space probe finds 69 hidden products (draft/pending/private/trash), including 60 in the 2025-11-15 import range (71–132) and 1029 and 1032 after the last published product, and 452 IDs in 358–809 with no published product.
findings.detail: Each delete-and-recreate cycle gives the item a new gla_<id> and a new retailer_id. For Google that means a new offer that starts review from zero, with no click or conversion history, and Performance Max or listing groups keyed on item IDs lose continuity. For Meta, pixel content_ids from past ViewContent and AddToCart events no longer match catalog items, so retargeting audiences and product-level ad stats reset, and hard deletes can leave orphaned catalog items. The SKU is part of the Meta retailer_id, so merely fixing or adding SKUs (59 products currently have none and use wc_post_id_<id>) also re-keys the Meta items. The same applies to converting flavour clones into one variable product, because the variations get new IDs. Drafts and trashed clones also inflate wp_posts and wp_postmeta and leave orphaned attachments, which is the 'bagunça' the user described.
findings.recommendation: Policy for the new solution: never delete-and-recreate a product that still exists physically. Keep its ID, and handle restocks, price changes and content fixes as updates. Retire items by setting them out of stock, or 'Don't sync and show' plus a 301 redirect, rather than hard deletes. Do all ID-changing operations (duplicate merges, SKU normalisation, simple→variable conversion) once, in one planned migration window, followed by GLA 'Sync all products' and the Facebook reset/resync tool, with a before/after map of old→new IDs. Before the migration, export current Merchant Center and Commerce Manager item lists to capture the baseline.

findings.title: Descriptions contradict titles and images: wrong colour, wrong product line, 'choose flavour' on single-flavour items, inconsistent kit contents, health claims
findings.evidence: 957 'Cor Cinza', 967 'Cor Rosa' and 968 'Cor Verde' share one description saying 'design moderno na cor azul'. Saero listings 819/822/825/827 (titles 'Soju Coreano Lotte Saero ... Sem Açúcar') use the Chum Churum description ('O Lotte Chum Churum Soju 360ml ...'), and 831 'Kit Soju ... Sem Açúcar' says 'Kit Soju Coreano Lotte Chum Churum Sem Açúcar'. Simple single-flavour products 810, 813, 815, 817, 819, 825, 827 list 12 flavours and say '1 Garrafa ... (escolha o sabor no momento da compra)', but there is no flavour selector. 829 says 'O Kit Contém 5/6 Garrafas', then '6 Garrafas', then 'Envio sortido, conforme disponibilidade'. 1011 says 'Peso líquido: 140g', but its images are named '...174g'. Health claims: Milkis 67/277–285 'entrega saúde'; O'Rice 69/263/265 'snack saudável e sem culpa', 'baixa caloria'; O'Star 149/231–237 'baixa caloria'. Meta description spec: 'Make sure the description matches the title and image for that specific product.' Google description: 'Ensure information provided here is consistent with other details ... and on your landing pages' and 'Describe only the product itself.' Google Misrepresentation: 'Offers that prompt customers to initiate a purchase ... without first providing all relevant information.'
findings.detail: These are content errors, not style problems. A customer buying 'Cinza' reads 'azul'. A customer buying Saero reads about Chum Churum. A customer buying 810 is told to choose a flavour at checkout when they cannot. Such mismatches are grounds for disapproval (Google editorial 'Unclear relevance', Misrepresentation) and for rejected Meta items. They come from copy-pasting or cloning one AI text across a family and editing only the title. The nutrition and health wording ('saúde', 'sem culpa', 'baixa caloria') is unsubstantiated for sugary sodas and fried snacks.
findings.recommendation: Generate descriptions from structured, per-SKU facts (brand, line, flavour, colour, net content, pack count) through a template or model that is only allowed to use those facts. Add a consistency validator: the colour, flavour, line and weight tokens in the title must appear in the description and must not conflict with any other value in it. Ban health claims unless they come from the label. Fix the listed products first.

findings.title: Titles carry the store name, pipe-separated keyword chains and 'Koreia, Kpop' stuffing; 62 titles exceed Meta's 65-character guidance
findings.evidence: 44 titles contain the store name ('Mimos Korea', 'Mimos Korea Design', 'Importação Mim...' or 'Premium Mimos'), for example 902 'Bala Gelatina Sakuragi 4D 50% Fruta 50g Sabor Maçã | Importado | Mimos Korea Design'. 45 titles use '|' chains ('Importado | Coreano | Mimos Korea'). Keyword stuffing appears in 810/813/815/817 ('..., Koreia, Kpop'), 1016 ('| Ceral, Crocante, Divertido e Delicioso |') and 864 ('Salgadinho Crocante, Divertido e Delicioso'). The flavour is pushed behind pipes in 1019/1021 ('| Snack Sabor Bife NY'). 62 of 103 titles are over 65 characters; none exceeds 150. Google title (6324415): 'Don't include promotional text. Don't add information such as price ... or your company's name'; 'avoid gimmicky ways of drawing attention such as all caps, symbols'. Meta title spec: 'Don't include extra words or keyword stuffing', and 'We recommend using less than 65 characters'.
findings.detail: The store name in the title wastes the visible part of the title and breaks Google's rule. Pipe chains read as keyword stuffing on Meta. The pattern is concentrated in the 2026 batches, which were written with ChatGPT for SEO. Titles in the 2025 batch are closer to spec, for example 'Biscoito Coreano Pepero Lotte 47g Sabor Original'.
findings.recommendation: Adopt one title template, for example '<Tipo> <Marca> <Linha> <Sabor/Cor> <Conteúdo> (<Pack>)', such as 'Salgadinho Orion O'Star Bife Americano 30 g'. Put the store name nowhere in titles. Put 'Importado' and 'Coreano' in attributes or product_type. Enforce ≤ 70 characters in the tool.

findings.title: Emoji-heavy, store-promotional descriptions (61 products) are sent as-is to Google and Meta
findings.evidence: Emoji appear in the description or short description of 61 products: all 59 created from 2026-08-22, plus 70 and 259 (for example 875/879 with 48 emoji each, 810–825 with 40). The descriptions include store promotion: 1011 '🛒 Por que comprar na Mimos Korea Design? 💖 Produtos 100% originais 📦 Envio rápido ... ⭐ Loja referência', 831 '✅ Envio rápido pela Mimos Korea Design', 810–829 '🇰🇷 Mimos Korea Design – Especialista em produtos importados ... 💜 감사합니다! (Kamsahamnida!)', and a hashtag block in 867 ('#CornChip #Orion ... #MimosKoreaDesign'). 1011 also has 'Aproveite'. The GLA FAQ says the WooCommerce long description is sent by default. Google description (6324468): 'Don't provide your business's history or policies'; 'Don't include promotional text such as ... shipping ... or your company's name'; 'avoid gimmicky ways of drawing attention such as all caps, symbols'. Google Editorial (6150244): 'Excessive or gimmicky use of numbers, letters, symbols, punctuation, emoticons, emoji'. Meta description: plain text, sentence case, no all caps.
findings.detail: Per the data caveat, HTML structure was not evaluated. The problem is the text itself: emoji bullets, store self-promotion, shipping claims, hashtags and Korean sign-offs are all things Google's spec says to leave out of the description attribute, and they raise the risk of editorial disapproval. The older 2025 copy has no emoji but is generic, templated AI prose ('Invista no ... valor agregado que o tornam indispensável'), with no concrete product facts.
findings.recommendation: Keep the long description as clean plain Portuguese: what the product is, flavour, content, ingredients and allergens, origin, storage. Put brand and store messaging in theme blocks or site-wide text, not in the product description. If emoji are wanted on the storefront, keep them out of the synced description, or use the GLA short-description filter or a Meta rich_text_description built from clean fields. The tool's validator should reject emoji, hashtags, URLs, store names and shipping promises in feed-bound fields.

findings.title: AI-written titles and descriptions are not declared as AI (structured_title / structured_description)
findings.evidence: The user states that inventory copy is produced with ChatGPT. The text shows it: repeated template phrasing across the 2025 batch ('Invista no ... valor agregado que o tornam indispensável', 'Escolha o ... para adicionar um toque coreano'), and emoji-structured blocks across the 2026 batch. Google product data spec (7052112, 6324415, 6324468): 'All titles created using generative AI must be provided using the structured title [structured_title] attribute' with digital_source_type 'trained_algorithmic_media'. The same rule applies to descriptions via structured_description. The spec also notes that AI-label regulations exist in some jurisdictions.
findings.detail: Google for WooCommerce sends plain title and description. As generated, the catalog therefore declares AI-written text as human-written. Enforcement is not yet visible in the data, but it is a stated minimum requirement. The cleaner fix is to rewrite titles from structured facts (a deterministic template, which is not 'generative'). For generated descriptions, use a feed path that can send structured_description, such as a supplemental feed or Merchant API.
findings.recommendation: In the new pipeline, record for each text field whether it was AI-generated. Generate titles deterministically from attributes. For AI descriptions, have a person review them, and send them as structured_description with trained_algorithmic_media via a Merchant Center supplemental data source keyed on gla_<id>.

findings.title: No structured product details: 59 products with zero attributes, no nutrition table on any food, no ABV on new soju, material only in prose
findings.evidence: attributes = {} on all 59 products created from 2026-08-22 (810–1021). None of the 86 food and drink products has a nutrition table ('tabela nutricional', 'valor energético' and 'porção' are absent from all descriptions). The 2025 attributes hold only approximate or invented values: 'Calorias': ['Cerca de 150 kcal por pacote'], ['Cerca de 500 kcal por embalagem'], and 'Pepero ... amêndoas (dependendo do sabor)'. The new soju (810–831) have no ABV. Plush and backpack material appears only in prose (957: 'Material: Poliéster Premium'). No colour attribute exists on the colour variants 957/967/968 or 969/980/981. Meta catalog fields: 'When using category-specific fields ... For example, for beauty products, you could provide ingredients'; 'material' and 'color' fields are listed. Google spec: 'Incorrect, inaccurate, or missing product information can cause disapprovals, limited eligibility'.
findings.detail: This is the 'sem detalhes (tabela nutricional, material)' problem the user described. Feeds cannot show facts that do not exist as fields, and the AI copy fills the gap with vague or wrong claims (see the gluten and health-claim findings). For imported packaged food sold in Brazil, customers expect the Portuguese label data: ingredients, allergens, nutrition per portion and validity. Brazilian labelling regulation was not fetched in this audit.
findings.recommendation: Define a per-category attribute schema in the new tool. Food: net_content, ingredients, allergens (contém/pode conter glúten, leite, soja, amendoim...), nutrition per 100 g and per portion, origin_country, importer, storage. Alcohol: ABV, age warning. Plush and backpacks: material, dimensions, colour, age range. Make the required fields block publishing. Map them to Meta color/material/additional_variant_attribute and to Google product_detail.

findings.title: Invalid price and default shipping weights/dimensions (R$0.00 in-stock soju; 25–29 L backpacks at 0.3 kg, 5×5×10 cm)
findings.evidence: 156 'Soju Chum-Churum Lotte Pêssego de 360ml' has price_brl 0.0, is in stock, and has no weight or dimensions. The dimensions 5×5×10 cm appear on 33 products, including the backpacks 957/967/968 (25 L, 'aprox. 45 cm x 32 cm', 0.3 kg) and 969/980/981 (29 L, 0.3 kg). 985 and 993 are 0.3–0.4 kg at 6×6×12 cm. Kit 829 (6 bottles) is 3.5 kg but 8×6×21 cm, the size of one bottle; kit 831 is 2.5 kg at 8×5×21 cm. Google price: 'Submit an amount and currency that match the price on your landing page and the checkout pages' (disapproval if not). Meta: shipping_weight is a catalog field. Infixs Correios Automatico quotes from weight and dimensions.
findings.detail: A zero or empty price on a live item is either disapproved or unbuyable (Google, Meta), and it is alcohol. The placeholder dimensions make Correios quotes wrong. Backpacks and multi-bottle kits will be undercharged at checkout, which hits the margin, and any carrier-calculated shipping in Merchant Center will disagree with checkout. A shipping mismatch is also a Merchant Center issue.
findings.recommendation: Set a price or unpublish 156. Measure the real packed weight and dimensions per SKU, and make them required, with sanity rules such as weight ≥ net content and backpacks > 0.5 kg. Store the pack count for kits and derive their dimensions.

findings.title: Flavour and colour variants modelled as unrelated simple products; some titles do not identify the variant
findings.evidence: 21 variant families are stored as separate simple products with no item_group_id, for example Milkis ×6, O'Star ×9 (with duplicates), Pepero ×4, Saero ×4, Yantai ×4, Sakuragi 4D ×3, backpacks 957/967/968 and 969/980/981. Titles 151 'Snack de Batata Coreano Orion Tok 38g Sabores' and 160 'Topokki Yopokki Youngpoong Coreano 120g Copo Sabores' do not say which flavour is sold. Google title: 'Distinguish between variants ... For product design elements that don't have a corresponding attribute, such as "flavor", add them to the title.' Google image: 'Submit a unique image that represents the distinguishing details of each variant.' Meta supports item_group_id and additional_variant_attribute 'Flavor:Strawberry'.
findings.detail: Simple products per flavour are acceptable to both channels if each has a unique title, image, SKU and GTIN. Grouping improves Meta's product pages and Google variant handling. Converting to WooCommerce variable products would create new variation IDs, and therefore new gla_ and retailer IDs (see the ID-stability finding). Titles like 151 and 160 are ambiguous: a buyer cannot know which flavour arrives.
findings.recommendation: Decide the model once. Either keep simple products with unique SKU and GTIN and optionally send item_group_id through a supplemental feed, or migrate to variable products during the single planned migration window. Fix 151 and 160 so they sell a specific flavour, or turn them into proper variants.

findings.title: Category taxonomy problems that leak into feeds (promo category on 64 products, soju outside 'Soju', 'Mamadeira' drinks)
findings.evidence: 'Ofertas Mimos' (a promotional bucket) is assigned to 64 products. 815 (soju) lacks the 'Soju' category. Chuyin drinks 833/838/840 are titled 'Mamadeira Chuyin 280ml Vidro | Bebida Cremosa' (mamadeira = baby bottle); the description says 'Mamadeira Iogurte ... Design retrô estilo mamadeira'. Plush 135–142 sit in 'Bebê e Infantil', and slippers 131 in 'Moda'.
findings.detail: Plugins may derive product_type and category-based sync rules from WooCommerce categories, and a promo bucket as a category is noise. The 815 gap would defeat category-based alcohol exclusion. A drink titled 'Mamadeira' risks Google auto-categorising it as a baby bottle (Baby & Toddler), a category and relevance mismatch.
findings.recommendation: Separate merchandising collections (offers) from the product taxonomy, using tags or a custom taxonomy for offers. Make the category mandatory and single-primary. Retitle 833/838/840 as 'Bebida Láctea Chuyin ... 280 ml (garrafa de vidro formato mamadeira)'.

limitations:
1. Public data only. The analysis used the local snapshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mimoskorea-stock/4368d5d2-795e-5742-b584-181afca38e4d/scratchpad/wf/catalog_full.json (103 published simple products), plus /home/user/mimoskorea-stock/audit/data/raw/wp_media.json and audit/data/derived/id_space.json for attachment parents and the hidden-ID probe. There was no wp-admin, database, Merchant Center or Commerce Manager access, so I could not confirm whether Google for WooCommerce or Facebook for WooCommerce is actually connected and syncing, which items are disapproved today, or whether GTINs exist in fields the Store API does not expose (_global_unique_id, _wc_gla_gtin).
2. Images were judged by file name and name_class only; no pixels, dimensions or embedded metadata were inspected. The 350×350 size for 894 is inferred from Amazon's URL suffix. The AI-image metadata status (IPTC DigitalSourceType) is unverified.
3. Per the stated caveat, HTML structure was not assessed; only the text was.
4. The Yoast Duplicate Post attribution is an inference. The shared SKUs, identical copied fields, sub-minute creation times and image ID = product ID + 1 fit a raw-meta clone and rule out WooCommerce's native duplicate, which generates unique SKUs. But Yoast's docs say products must be explicitly enabled for Duplicate Post, and other raw-meta paths leave the same fingerprint. Confirmation needs the '_dp_original' postmeta query.
5. That clones inherit Facebook and Google sync IDs (fb_product_item_id, _wc_gla_google_ids), and that deleting a clone could then delete the original's channel item, is reasoned from plugin source and docs, not observed. The WooCommerce set_sku uniqueness check is inferred from the analogous set_global_unique_id code seen in the same file.
6. Several sources (marked 'search-highlight only') were read via Exa search excerpts rather than full-page fetches. The Meta image-spec help page was truncated by the fetcher, so the 500×500 minimum is cited from Meta's developer catalog-fields page.
7. Brazilian law is cited only where fetched (Lei 9.294/1996 art. 1; Lei 13.106/2015). Lei 10.674/2003 (gluten labelling) and ANVISA labelling rules are mentioned but were not fetched. None of this is legal advice.
8. The soju ABV values (12% stated on 154–156) and the Choco Pie manufacturer (Orion vs Lotte) were not verified against manufacturer data.
